title: Unit 7 test: Differential Equations
author: ab-3
directions: This practice test has two sections. Section I is multiple choice: Part A without a calculator and Part B with a graphing calculator. Section II is free response: Part A with a graphing calculator and Part B without one. Show your work on free-response questions; answers without supporting work may not earn full credit. Unless a question says otherwise, angles are in radians, exact answers are expected without a calculator, and calculator answers are given to three decimal places. Results are raw points for practice only.

figures.alt: A slope field drawn at points spaced 0.5 apart for −3 ≤ x ≤ 2 and −2 ≤ y ≤ 2. Segments are horizontal along the vertical line x = −1 and along the x-axis. To the right of x = −1 the segments rise above the x-axis and fall below it; to the left of x = −1 they fall above the x-axis and rise below it. Segments are steeper farther from these two lines.
Coordinate axes with a grid and nine dots at the points with x = −1, 0, 1 and y = 0, 1, 2.
The nine grid points with slope segments for dy/dx = x^2(1 − y): slope 1 at (−1, 0) and (1, 0); slope 0 at (0, 0), at all three points with y = 1, and at (0, 2); slope −1 at (−1, 2) and (1, 2).

parts.directions: Choose the best answer. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: A town has 5000 residents. The number N of residents who have heard a piece of news increases at a rate proportional to the number of residents who have not yet heard it. Which differential equation models N, where k is a positive constant?
items.rationale: The residents who have not heard are 5000 − N, and "rate proportional to" means dN/dt = k(5000 − N).

distractorNotes.B: Makes the rate proportional to those who have heard.
distractorNotes.C: Makes the rate proportional to the product of both groups, which is not what is described.
distractorNotes.D: Sets N itself, not its rate of change, proportional to 5000 − N.

items.prompt: Which function is a solution of the differential equation x·dy/dx = 3y for x > 0?
Which differential equation has the slope field shown?
items.rationale: Slopes are 0 along x = −1 and along y = 0, and they are positive for x > −1 and y > 0, which matches (x + 1)y/2.

distractorNotes.A: Would have horizontal segments along x = 1, not x = −1.
distractorNotes.B: Would have horizontal segments along x = 0 and y = −1.
distractorNotes.D: Has the right zero lines but the opposite sign everywhere.

items.prompt: Let y = f(x) be the solution of dy/dx = y^2 − x with f(1) = 2. At x = 1, the graph of f is

distractorNotes.A: Both signs are wrong: the slope is 3 and the second derivative is 11.
distractorNotes.C: Differentiating y^2 gives 2y·dy/dx, which makes d^2y/dx^2 positive.

items.prompt: Which is the general solution of dy/dx = (y + 2)/x^2 for x > 0?
items.rationale: dy/(y + 2) = x^(−2) dx gives ln|y + 2| = −1/x + C, so y + 2 = Ae^(−1/x).

distractorNotes.C: Adds the constant after exponentiating and drops the −2.
distractorNotes.D: Does not integrate; it keeps 1/x^2 as a factor.

items.prompt: Let y = f(x) be the solution of dy/dx = xy^2 with f(0) = 1. What is f(1)?
items.rationale: y^(−2) dy = x dx gives −1/y = x^2/2 + C; f(0) = 1 gives C = −1, so y = 2/(2 − x^2) and f(1) = 2.

distractorNotes.A: Uses the tangent line at x = 0, where the slope is 0, instead of solving.
distractorNotes.B: Solves −1/1 = 0 + C as C = 1, giving −1/y = 3/2 at x = 1.
distractorNotes.C: Drops the negative sign from integrating y^(−2), giving 1/y = x^2/2 + 1.

items.prompt: A substance decays at a rate proportional to the amount present. After 30 years, 1/8 of the original amount remains. What is its half-life?
items.rationale: 1/8 = (1/2)^3, so 30 years is three half-lives: 10 years each.

distractorNotes.A: Halves 30 instead of finding how many halvings give 1/8.

items.prompt: Which line is a solution of the differential equation dy/dx = x − 2y?

parts.directions: Choose the best answer. A graphing calculator is required for some questions. If the exact value is not a choice, choose the closest approximation.

items.prompt: A town's population grows at a rate proportional to its size. It was 12,000 in 2020 and 15,500 in 2026. To the nearest person, what does the model predict for 2030?

distractorNotes.A: Assumes linear growth of 3500 every 6 years.
distractorNotes.B: Multiplies 15,500 by the 6-year growth factor, a 6-year step, not 4 years.
distractorNotes.C: Projects 10 years forward from 2026 instead of from 2020.

items.prompt: Let y = f(x) be the solution of dy/dx = y^2 cos x with f(0) = 0.5. What is f(2)?
items.rationale: −1/y = sin x + C with C = −2, so y = 1/(2 − sin x) and f(2) = 1/(2 − sin 2) ≈ 0.917.

distractorNotes.B: Uses 1/(2 + sin x), a sign error in the constant.
distractorNotes.C: Reports 2 − sin 2, the reciprocal of the answer.
distractorNotes.D: Uses −1/(2 + sin x), losing the sign when solving for y.

items.prompt: Let y = f(x) be the solution of dy/dx = ln(x + y) with f(1) = 2. Using the line tangent to the graph of f at x = 1, what is the approximation of f(1.3)?

distractorNotes.B: This is the slope ln 3, not the approximate value.
distractorNotes.D: Uses a step of 0.6 instead of 0.3.

items.prompt: A pan at 95 °C cools in a 22 °C kitchen according to dT/dt = −k(T − 22), where t is in minutes. After 10 minutes the pan is at 70 °C. At what time does it reach 40 °C?

distractorNotes.A: Assumes the temperature falls at a constant 2.5 °C per minute.
distractorNotes.C: Ignores the kitchen temperature and uses T = 95e^(−kt).
distractorNotes.D: Gives the time after the 10-minute reading rather than from t = 0.

parts.directions: A graphing calculator is required. Show the setup for every calculator result, and give answers to three decimal places with units.

items.prompt: A pesticide residue on a field breaks down at a rate proportional to the amount present, so dR/dt = −kR, where R is the amount in kilograms, t is time in weeks, and k > 0. Measurements show 140 kg of residue at t = 2 and 95 kg at t = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use separation of variables to show that R(t) = Ce^(−kt) for some constant C.

rubric.criterion: Integrates to ln|R| = −kt + C1 and exponentiates to R = Ce^(−kt).

parts.answer: dR/R = −k dt, so ln R = −kt + C1 (R > 0) and R = e^(C1)e^(−kt) = Ce^(−kt).
steps: Separate, integrate both sides, then exponentiate; C = e^(C1).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the values of k and C.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At what time will 40 kg of residue remain?

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find dR/dt at t = 5. Using correct units, explain what this value means.

rubric.criterion: Interprets: at t = 5 weeks the residue is decreasing at about 12.279 kilograms per week.

parts.answer: dR/dt ≈ −12.279 kg/week: at week 5 the residue is decreasing at about 12.279 kilograms per week.
steps: Use the differential equation directly: dR/dt = −kR with R(5) = 95.

parts.directions: No calculator is allowed. Show your work and give exact answers.

items.prompt: Consider the differential equation dy/dx = x^2(1 − y).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On the axes provided, sketch a slope field for the differential equation at the nine points indicated.

rubric.criterion: Horizontal segments at the three points with y = 1 and at the points with x = 0.
Slope 1 at (−1, 0) and (1, 0) and slope −1 at (−1, 2) and (1, 2), drawn with the correct signs.

parts.answer: See the completed slope field: slopes 1, 0, 1 in the row y = 0; 0, 0, 0 in the row y = 1; and −1, 0, −1 in the row y = 2 (for x = −1, 0, 1).
steps: Evaluate x^2(1 − y) at each point.
x^2 ≥ 0, so the sign of each slope is the sign of 1 − y.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let y = f(x) be the particular solution with f(1) = 3. Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of f at x = 1, and use it to approximate f(1.1).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find d^2y/dx^2 at the point (1, 3). Is the approximation in part (b) an overestimate or an underestimate? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Overestimate, because the graph of f is concave down near x = 1, so the tangent line lies above it.

parts.answer: d^2y/dx^2 = −2; overestimate, since f is concave down near x = 1.
steps: Product rule: d/dx [x^2(1 − y)] = 2x(1 − y) + x^2(−dy/dx).

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find y = f(x), the particular solution with f(1) = 3.

rubric.criterion: Separates: dy/(1 − y) = x^2 dx (or dy/(y − 1) = −x^2 dx).
Uses f(1) = 3 and solves: y = 1 + 2e^((1 − x^3)/3).

steps: y − 1 > 0 at the start, so y − 1 = 2e^((1 − x^3)/3).
